bottom_line: GA0602400 should use a near-exact ATL airport-campus footprint built from official ATL Airfield, Surface Transportation, and Buildings ArcGIS polygons, validated and closed on the Clayton side with City of Atlanta airport parcels.

official_scope_support.summary: ATL is the City of Atlanta's airport campus, so the production overlap should track airport property/operations surfaces rather than Atlanta city limits or a county proxy.

explicit_exclusions: Fulton County-only or Clayton County-only proxy
all parcels in Clayton appraisal area 333
airport-adjacent Airport South Parkway warehouse parcels not owned by the City of Atlanta

atl_arcgis.interpretation: The ATL ArcGIS organization publishes airport-specific polygon layers for airfield operations, parking, roads, buildings, and bridge structures. Those official surfaces provide the primary operational geometry for the campus.

clayton_parcels.interpretation: Clayton parcel QA is used conservatively: only City of Atlanta-owned parcels within 200 m of the official ATL footprint and within the contiguous airport-campus parcel component are added. Airport-address parcels held by private warehouse owners and non-contiguous City of Atlanta edge parcels are recorded and excluded rather than silently swept into the footprint.

published_acres_crosscheck.interpretation: The final footprint sits close to ATL's widely published ~4,700-acre campus size, which is consistent with a production-usable near-exact airport footprint built from operational geometry rather than a single legal boundary polygon.

build_method.seed_geometry: Union the official ATL Airfield polygon layers (Apron, DeicingArea, Infield, MovementArea, RunwaySafetyAreaBoundary, RW_TW_SafetyZoneMerge, AirOperationsArea) with official ATL ParkingLot, Building, NonCOABuildings, and FireStations polygons.
build_method.parcel_fill: Add Clayton parcels only where OWNERNME resolves to City of Atlanta, the parcel lies within 200 m of the official ATL seed geometry, and it belongs to the contiguous parcel component anchored on seed-touching airport parcels.
build_method.roadway_fill: Clip official ATL RoadSegment and Bridges polygons to a 120 m buffer around the contiguous parcel-backed campus so airport roadway structures are retained without importing the broader metro street network.
why_this_is_defensible: The official ATL GIS surfaces are stronger than passenger-facing maps because they encode operational polygons directly.
City-owned Clayton parcels close gaps on the south/cargo side while filtering out nearby non-airport industrial properties that happen to share the airport appraisal area.
Road and bridge polygons must be clipped because the raw services spill well beyond the airport, but clipped segments are still official ATL geometry rather than inferred buffers.
omissions_by_design: No non-City Airport South Parkway warehouse parcels are included.
No attempt is made to fabricate a single legal property-boundary polygon that ATL does not publish publicly.
No off-property police authority or mutual-aid geography is modeled.

residual_caveats: This remains a near-exact footprint because ATL does not appear to publish one public whole-property legal-boundary polygon.
Clayton parcel QA improves the south/cargo side, but no comparable public Fulton parcel layer was folded in here; the northern side relies on official ATL operational geometry.
If ATL later publishes a single airport-boundary parcel or campus polygon, this packet should be regenerated from that authoritative surface.
